# Review — aeneid-042 (Aeneid VI.190–294), adversarial reviewer

Two passes. Pass 1: every unit's `l`, `i`, `n` checked against the Latin word by word, along with every grammatical label, the speech marks, the misprint handling (rule 5b), the doubtful claims and the mythology, and every `i` checked for remembered English. Pass 2: re-read the edited units. Then hand-scanned all 105 lines by quantities, not only the flagged one, and compared each line with the scanner's output, run in-process exactly as `build_aeneid.py` runs `SL.scan_story`. Every new `scan-fixes.json` entry was checked against the build's word-match rule and a replica of the validator's six-foot rule. `t` is untouched: `make_units.py` cut tuples are unchanged and all 44 units are still cut by `aeneid_lib.cut`. `units.json` was regenerated by `make_units.py`; `build_aeneid.py` was not run. Speech marks: `t` 4 “ and 4 ”, `l` 4/4 (the extra pair is the quoted name “Misenus”), `i` 3/3. Speeches open at 194, 258 and 259 and close at 197, 258 and 261.

**Severity counts: major 4, medium 11, low 17. Refused findings: 10 (listed at the end).**

## Changes

### Major
1. **6.210 scan wrong** (cost 0.0, unflagged). The scanner split Aeneas (A-e-ne) and gave `avidus` a long *vi*. Hand scansion: Cor-ri-pit | Ae-ne | as ex | tem(plo) a-vi | dus-que re | frin-git.
2. **6.212 scan wrong** (unflagged). The scanner made Mī-sē-num short-short and split Teucri (Te-u). Both syllables of Mīsēnus are long (6.164, 6.234). Hand scansion: Nec mi-nus | in-te-re | a Mi | se(num) in | li-to-re | Teu-cri.
3. **6.280 scan wrong** (unflagged). The scanner read `ferreique` as fer-re-i with a short *i*, a dactyl the long nominative-plural *-ī* cannot make. Hand scansion with synizesis: fer-rei | Eu-me-ni | dum tha-la | (mi) et Dis | cor-di-a | de-mens. This confirms the drafter's note.
4. **Note 286–289 (Scyllae biformes)**: "a girl above and sea-dogs below, as in Odyssey 12" is false. Homer's Scylla has six heads on long necks. The girl-and-sea-beast form is the later picture, which Virgil gives at III.426–432. Fixed.

### Medium
5–10. **Scan, unflagged scanner errors (cost 0.0)**:
   - 6.223: `subiectam` was read su-bi-ec-tam with a vowel *i*. The *i* is consonantal after the prefix (sub | iec | tam), as at 2.721.
   - 6.227: `reliquias` was forced into synizesis (reliqu-ias). It is rē-lĭ-quĭ-ās, as at 1.30, 1.598, 4.343 and 5.47. This confirms the drafter's "long first syllable".
   - 6.232: Aeneas was split (A-e-ne).
   - 6.250: Aeneas and Eumenidum were both split (A-e-ne, E-u-me). Fix: Ae-ne | as ma(tri) | Eu-me-ni | dum mag | nae-que so | ro-ri.
   - 6.261: the vocative Aenea was split. Fix: Ae-nē | ā nunc.
   - 6.291: Aeneas was split.

   Hand scansions were added for all six.
11. **Note 232–235, misprint form**: the note said "corrected here in l" and did not say that `t` keeps the print. It now opens in the house form used for 6.155 in aeneid-041: "The print has '“Misenus ”ab', a misprint for '“Misenus” ab', corrected here. … t keeps the print, while l closes the quotation after 'Misenus'."
12. **Note 249–251, misprint form**: same fix for `tibi. Proserpina`. The note now says "corrected here … t keeps the print, while l and i read the comma." The 6.197 notes (units 196–197 and 197–198) already matched aeneid-041's wording word for word; they are left.
13. **Note 242–244 (bracketed line)**: "missing from most of the oldest manuscripts" is not something I can confirm from the permitted references. It is softened to "Greenough prints it as spurious, as many editors do: it reads like a learned gloss on the lines before, explaining the name."
14. **Note 232–235 (Cape Misenum)**: "in Virgil's day the base of the Roman fleet" is doubtful, because the fleet's move to Misenum is hard to date before Virgil's death. Changed to "under Augustus the chief base of the Roman fleet".
15. **Note 237–241 (sese … ferebat)**: the note said `ferebat` "is used without an object" with `sese` taken only with `effundens`. Now: `sese` serves both `effundens` and `ferebat` ("carried itself", rose).

### Low
16. i 220: "The cry of mourning goes up." was the only present tense in a past-tense narrative. It is now "A cry of mourning went up."
17. Note 220: the claim that the Romans called this groan the *conclamatio* was not secure (that was the calling of the dead man's name). Removed.
18. i 224–225: "The heaped offerings burn" became "were burned" (tense). "Flowing" for `fuso` became "poured".
19. Note 229–231: `novissima verba` was given flatly as "'vale'". It now gives the farewell, or (as some old commentators took it) the formula that dismissed the mourners.
20. Note 249–251: "her great sister, Earth, as in Hesiod's account" implied that Hesiod calls them sisters. It now says that in Hesiod both Earth and Night are among the first powers to come into being.
21. Note 263: "either way the boldness is his as much as hers" was muddled. It now spells out both constructions: with `aequat` he matches her with bold steps; with `vadentem` she strides boldly and he keeps up.
22. Note 266–267: `numine vestro` was labelled "ablative of cause". It is now "ablative of accordance".
23. i 266–267: "let it be, with your consent, that I lay bare …" was stiff. It is now "may I, by your leave, lay bare what lies sunk deep in the earth and the dark!"
24. i 237–241 (the cave): it echoed known versions ("sheltered by a black lake and the gloom of the woods", "wing its way"). Rephrased: "… guarded by a black lake and the darkness of the forest; no bird could fly over it and live, so deadly was the breath …".
25. i 258–259: "Away, away, you uninitiated" echoed a well-known version. It is now "Keep off, keep far off, all you who are not initiated".
26. i 264–266: "Gods who hold dominion over souls" echoed a well-known version. It is now "Gods whose rule is over the souls of the dead … may heaven's law allow me to tell what I have heard".
27. i 268–269 (*Ibant obscuri*): "On they went, dim …, through the empty halls of Dis" echoed. It is now "Unseen they walked under the lonely night through the gloom, through the vacant halls of Dis and his kingdom of empty things".
28. i 270–272: "black night has taken the colour from the world" echoed. It is now "has drained all things of their colour".
29. i 278–281: "Sleep, Death's own brother" echoed. It is now "Sleep, of one blood with Death", which matches the note's gloss of `consanguineus`.
30. i 282–284 (elm of Dreams): "make their home in throngs, clinging under every leaf" was a close echo. It is now "there, men say, idle Dreams roost everywhere, hanging beneath each leaf".
31. i 286–289 (monster list): the i ran word for word with a well-known version, including "hissing horribly … armed with flame … the shape of the three-bodied shade". It is rewritten as real English: "Scyllas, half girl, half beast, … the Lernaean monster with its fearful hiss, the Chimaera bristling with fire, … and the ghost of the giant with three bodies".
32. i 290–294: "thin, bodiless lives flitting in a hollow semblance of form … cleave/slash … shadows" echoed. It is now "frail lives with no bodies, fluttering about in the empty likeness of a shape, … hacked uselessly at shadows with his blade".

## Scan-fixes lines added (9)
6.210, 6.212, 6.223, 6.227, 6.232, 6.250, 6.261, 6.280 and 6.291 were appended at the end of `scan-fixes.json`, each with its reason. Each entry matches the line's words under `WORD_RE` and has six feet (five dactyls or spondees, then –× or ⏑×), 14–15 syllables and one ×. This was checked by a replica of the build's and the validator's rules. The file's existing entries are unchanged (diff: 99 lines added).

## Hand-scan results for the flagged and special lines
- **6.242** (packet flag, COSTLY 2.0): the scanner is right, so there is no entry. un-de lo | cum Gra | i di | xe-runt | no-mi-n(e) A | or-non. Grāī is two long syllables, dīxērunt is long-long, and Ăornon has a short alpha-privative A with *or* long by position. Hiatus at *nomine Aornon* gives no hexameter, so the elision is forced.
- **Greek eu**: Teucri at 212 (fixed) and Eumenidum at 250 (fixed). At 280 the scanner had Eu- right; the line was wrong only for *ferrei*. Briareus at 287 is Bri-a-reus with *-eus* in synizesis; the scanner is correct.
- **Initial Ae-**: Aeneas/Aenea at 210, 232, 250, 261 and 291 were all split by the scanner and all are fixed. aeternum (235), aequat (263) and aëno/aëna/aërio (Ae- with diaeresis: ă-ē-nus, ā-ĕ-rĭ-us; 218, 228, 234) are correct. āĕra (202) is correct.
- **Consonantal i after a prefix**: subiectam (223) is fixed. coniciunt (222, read cōn-ĭ-cĭ-unt) and subiere (222, sub + *i*re, a true vowel) are correct. iuga (256), iuvencos (243) and Iuppiter (272) are correct.
- **Synizesis**: ferrei (280) and reliquias (227) are fixed. Harpyiae (289) is Har-pȳ-iae, as at 3.212, and is correct. malesuada (276, *sua* one syllable) is correct.
- **Elision and hiatus**: Tuque O (196), via est (194), O procul (258, O not elided), se immisit (262) and sese halitus (240) are all correct.
- **Muta cum liquida lengthenings** forced by the metre: nigro (238), nigrantis (243), sacris (246), feretro (222). All are correct.
- All other lines: hand quantities agree with the scanner's marks.

## Refused findings
- **R1 (low) — 6.242 scan-fixes entry.** Considered because the line was flagged. Refused, as the scanner's scansion is the only fit and is correct.
- **R2 (low) — misprinted marks still visible in `t`** (`parens. ”Sic`, `“Misenus ”ab`, `tibi. Proserpina`). `t` must match the pinned source, so the reader's Latin line still shows the print. `l`/`i` carry the corrected reading, and each note opens with the print's reading. This is the same as aeneid-041 R1. Re-pinning the source is the owner's call.
- **R3 (low) — Harpyiae 289 and Briareus 287.** Checked by hand. The scanner is right and there is no entry.
- **R4 (low) — note 199–200, `possent`** "subjunctive because the limit is the doves' own design". This is a defensible reading (the limit as the birds' intent), so it is kept.
- **R5 (low) — note 192–193 records the variant `agnovit`** although it does not change the sense. It is harmless and kept.
- **R6 (low) — note 255–258, the `limina` variant.** It only reports that The Latin Library prints it and glosses it. It makes no claim about which reading is right, so it is kept.
- **R7 (low) — note 226–228, `reliquias` with a long first syllable.** Confirmed: Virgil's rēliquiae, the *relliquiae* spelling. Kept.
- **R8 (low) — note 224–225, `fuso … olivo` "ablative of description".** Some take it as ablative absolute, but the label is defensible. Kept.
- **R9 (low) — i 273–274 "Grief and the avenging Cares have made their beds".** This is close to the literal sense of `posuere cubilia` and has no distinctive wording, so it is kept.
- **R10 (low) — the mythological claims checked and kept**: Briareus as the hundred-hander of Iliad 1; the Chimaera of Iliad 6; the Lernaean hydra killed by Hercules; the Gorgons; the Harpies of Book III; Geryon as the three-bodied shade; the Centaurs; Patroclus's funeral (Iliad 23: wine on the pyre, bones gathered) and his washing and anointing (Iliad 18); Elpenor's oar (Odyssey 11–12); Aornos as "birdless"; Sleep and Death as twins (Homer) and children of Night (Hesiod).
